{{Quote|Master! I've just encountered some kind of assassin droid, armed with a new weapon, a cortosis sword.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="SW:OW" />}}
The '''Trade Federation assassin droid''' was a model of [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] used by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] during their [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. The [[Droid/Legends|droids]] were [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in appearance and carried [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]] weapons. They fought the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] during the invasion.

==Description==
A model of [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]], the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]]<ref name="State of the Arts">{{GamerCite|8|State of the Arts}}</ref> was [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] in appearance and had [[Color/Legends|red]] and black<ref name="SW:OW" /> [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]] alloy chassis shell that provided some resistance to [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] attacks,<ref name="State of the Arts" /> as well as a pair of red [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]].<ref name="SW:OW" /> They carried [[Cortosis sword/Legends|cortosis blades]] or cortosis maces, and were constructed to kill [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]],<ref name="SW:OW guide">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> the peacekeepers of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="SWE1 crawl" /> The cortosis weapons were able to block lightsabers, the Jedi weapon.<ref name="SW:OW" />

==History==
When the Trade Federation,<ref name="SW:OW" /> a [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning corporation,<ref name="SWE1 crawl">{{Film|I}}</ref> [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invaded]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]<ref name="SW:OW" /> in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] in response to a [[Senate Resolution BR-0371|trade dispute]],<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' establishes that the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] took place in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> Trade Federation [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] droids were deployed as part of the invasion [[Army/Legends|army]]. An assassin droid had its first encounter with the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] after two [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] were sent to negotiate an end to the invasion and were forced to escape a Trade Federation ambush by stowing onboard a [[Unidentified C-9979 landing craft|C-9979 landing craft]]. The Jedi [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] quickly [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|dispatched]] the droid.<ref name="SW:OW" />

More Trade Federation assassin droids [[Capture of Theed/Legends|dueled]] with Kenobi and his [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] on the planet's surface while they tried to meet with Naboo's [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], but were also destroyed. The Jedi later decided to escort her off-planet to travel to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. When the Queen returned to Naboo shortly afterward, Kenobi agreed to [[Rescue mission in Theed|rescue]] several [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Naboo Security Force]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]]. Kenobi encountered and destroyed more of the droids during that mission. Eventually the Trade Federation was defeated on the planet.<ref name="SW:OW" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Swow_assassin_concept.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Concept art from the strategy guide]]
The Trade Federation assassin droid was first mentioned in a preview in the "[[State of the Arts]]" department in [[Star Wars Gamer 7|''Star Wars Gamer'' 7]],<ref name="Gamer">{{GamerCite|7|State of the Arts}}</ref> shipped to subscribers on [[October 16]], 2001.<ref name="Fringe">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20011018.html|text=Live on the Fringe: ''Gamer'' # 7}}</ref> The assassin droids then appeared in the 2001 [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']].<ref name="SW:OW" /> Those carrying maces were referred to as "mace droids" in the [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|game's strategy guide]], and the droids as a whole received a small introduction in the guide.<ref name="SW:OW guide" />

In the game, there is an altered scene from the [[1999]] film ''[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]''. Two Trade Federation assassin droids escort Queen Amidala in the game instead of<ref name="SW:OW" /> [[OOM-series security droid/Legends|OOM battle droids]].<ref name="NEG Droids">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> This article assumes that portion of the game is [[Canon|non-canon]] in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.<ref name="SW:OW" />

The design of the Trade Federation assassin droid was derived from early [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] concept art developed by [[Doug Chiang]] for ''The Phantom Menace'',<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> dated to [[January 15]]th, [[1995]]. Its facial features, while clearly robotic, served as a nod to the [[Stormtrooper armor/Legends|helmets]] worn by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] in the [[original trilogy]].<ref name="Recycle">{{SW|url=news/5-early-star-wars-character-concepts|text=Yoda Almost Looked Like a Garden Gnome, Plus 4 More Early ''Star Wars'' Character Concepts}}</ref>
